title: PRD: degradation thresholds, graceful fallback rules, and rollback playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Update the product requirements document to convert the recent L3 latency incident's postmortem actions into concrete, testable product requirements. The goal is to define deterministic degradation thresholds, prioritized graceful-fallback behaviors, and explicit rollback/mitigation playbooks that the runtime and Console can consume. This PRD is scoped to: 1) observable thresholds and SLI->SLO mapping, 2) fallback policy spec (model variants, degraded features, cache priority), 3) automated rollout/rollback criteria surfaced in Console, and 4) documentation and acceptance tests for QA and SRE. Out of scope: underlying kernel-level optimizations and hardware SKU changes (handled in ENG tickets).
acceptance_criteria: S1: Documented degradation thresholds (latency p99, tail percent drop in throughput, error-rate delta) with numeric values and rationale
S2: A prioritized fallback policy table that maps failure modes to actions (e.g., degrade from full model -> quantized variant -> cached response), including expected cost/latency trade-offs
S3: Console UI/REST contract defined to expose active fallback state and allow manual rollback with audit trail
S4: Rollback/playbook steps enumerated for SRE/Customer Success, including communication templates and monitoring dashboards to confirm recovery
S5: Acceptance tests and e2e scenarios recorded in the PRD with links to test definitions that validate each fallback path and rollback trigger
S6: Linked ENG tickets for implementation work and SRE runbook ownership assigned
notes: Decision: Use a three-tier fallback model (full model -> cached prefix -> lightweight model) to balance quality and latency; avoid blind traffic shedding except under sustained capacity exhaustion
Trade-off: Enabling aggressive prefix caching reduces tokens served but may increase repeated stale outputs; mitigation is cache TTL and prompt-versioning
PM suggestion: Expose a per-customer 'degradation_tolerance' knob in Console to allow customers to prioritize cost vs. availability
Follow-up: Validate thresholds with synthetic load tests from ENG and canary traffic from Dedicated clusters
